comments: la-ti-abuseipdb v2 - AbuseIPDB blacklist to Microsoft Sentinel threat intelligence.
Pulls the AbuseIPDB blacklist once daily and publishes each IP as a STIX 2.1
indicator via the Sentinel threat-intelligence upload API. Indicators land in the
ThreatIntelIndicators table with ObservableKey 'ipv4-addr:value', which is what the
TI-matching analytics rules in this repo already join against.
DESIGN NOTES
- Uses plain HTTP actions with ManagedServiceIdentity auth rather than the Azure Key
Vault and Microsoft Sentinel managed connectors. This avoids creating any API
connection resources, so the playbook needs no interactive OAuth consent step and
deploys cleanly from source.
- runtimeConfiguration.secureData keeps the API key out of run history: secure
OUTPUTS on the Key Vault read (the response body is the secret) and secure INPUTS
on the AbuseIPDB call (the key travels in a request header). Without these, anyone
with Logic App read access can recover the key from a run.
- valid_until is deliberately short (7 days). AbuseIPDB confidence scores decay and
addresses get reassigned, so a long TTL produces false positives against stale
infrastructure. The daily run refreshes what is still listed.
- Get_Blacklist has retryPolicy 'none' on purpose. The AbuseIPDB free tier allows
only about 5 blacklist requests per day, so the default 4 exponential retries
would burn a day's quota on a single bad afternoon. A failed pull waits for
tomorrow instead.
- Upload_Stix_Objects keeps exponential retries. That endpoint is Azure-side, is
rate limited at 100 requests/minute, and returns 429 under load, so retrying is
the correct behaviour there.
- The upload API accepts a maximum of 100 objects per request, so indicators are
chunked and uploaded in batches. For_Each_Batch runs with concurrency 1: batches
are small, sequential execution stays far below the 100/minute limit, and a
failure is far easier to read in run history.
VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY, NOT ASSUMED (throwaway workflow, run, output inspected)
- guid() inside a Select is evaluated PER ITEM, so every indicator gets a distinct
id. Had it been evaluated once per run, a whole batch would collapse to a single
indicator. Ids are non-deterministic, so a repeat run creates new objects for an
IP rather than updating the old one; the 7-day TTL is what stops accumulation.
- The doubled single quotes in the pattern expression produce exactly
[ipv4-addr:value = '1.2.3.4'].
- chunk(array, 100) on 250 items yields 3 batches of 100/100/50, and chunk() on an
EMPTY array yields zero batches. That is why no explicit empty-data Condition is
needed: an empty blacklist makes For_Each_Batch a no-op rather than sending a
malformed upload.
- confidence is bound with @item() rather than @{item()} so it stays a JSON integer.
The upload API requires an integer in 0-100 and rejects a quoted string.
- trackedProperties were removed. Logic Apps rejects tracked properties that
reference other actions ('can only reference its own action's inputs and outputs,
trigger inputs and outputs and parameters'), and they only surface anywhere if the
workflow exports run diagnostics to Log Analytics. Run_Summary carries the same
information into run history instead.
PREREQUISITES
1. Key Vault secret 'AbuseIPDBApiKey' holding an AbuseIPDB API key.
2. The workflow's system-assigned identity granted 'Key Vault Secrets User' on the
vault.
3. The same identity granted 'Microsoft Sentinel Contributor' AT WORKSPACE SCOPE.
The upload API rejects identities that hold this role only at resource-group
scope.
AbuseIPDB free tier: the blacklist endpoint allows roughly 5 requests per day, so do
not schedule this more often than daily. confidenceMinimum is a subscriber-only
parameter but its default is already 100, so a free key returns only maximum
confidence addresses without passing it. limit is NOT subscriber-only and caps at
10,000 on the free tier.
COST NOTE: measured 916 billed bytes per indicator in ThreatIntelIndicators, and the
table is billable. At limit=1000 that is roughly 0.9 MB/day.
Set the two parameter defaults below before deploying.

select.name: @{concat('AbuseIPDB - ', item()?['ipAddress'])}
select.description: @{concat('AbuseIPDB blacklist entry. Abuse confidence score ', item()?['abuseConfidenceScore'], '. Last reported ', item()?['lastReportedAt'], '.')}
